section_summary.extract_value: This section concludes that self-compassion may protect young adult women from body image threats, suggesting that the amount of self-compassion relative to their usual level is important. The findings indicate that cultivating a higher-than-usual amount of self-compassion can help women cope with daily body image stressors.
section_summary.evidence_source: The present findings add to the growing body of literature suggesting that self-compassion may help to protect young adult women from potential body image threats. However, unlike past research, the current results show that young adult women may not need to be more self-compassionate than other women in order to be protected from exposure to recurrent body image threats. Also important is the amount of self-compassion they show themselves relative to their usual level on days when body image threats are higher than usual. Results suggest that teaching young adult women to respond to daily body image stressors by cultivating a higher-than-usual amount of self-compassion may enable them to function and feel better than they ordinarily would on those potentially stressful days.
